title: Package
description:
A downloadable `System` or `Module` listed in the content catalog.

A `Package` is catalog metadata, not installed content: it describes what is available,
where to download it and which app versions it supports. Installing one produces a
`System` or `Module` whose `package` field points back at the manifest, which is how
updates are detected later.

Unlike the Realm-backed containers, `Package` is a plain `Codable` value decoded straight
from the catalog JSON.

- SeeAlso: `System`, `Module`, `Compatibility`

id.description:
The unique identifier for this package.

A stable, author-chosen slug. It becomes the `id` of the installed `System` or
`Module`, and is what update checks match on.

## Examples
- `"dnd5e"`
- `"lost-mine-of-phandelver"`

name.description:
The display name of the package.

## Examples
- `"Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition"`

type.description:
Whether this package installs a system or a module.

- SeeAlso: `PackageType`, `contentType`

category.description:
The catalog category this package is listed under.

For module packages this mirrors `ModuleCategory`.

## Examples
- `"adventure"`, `"pack"`, `"rules"`, `"compendium"`

system.description:
The game system this package's content targets.

The `System/id` of the required system. `nil` for system packages themselves and for
system-agnostic content.

## Examples
- `"dnd5e"`

version.description:
The version offered by this catalog listing.

Compared against the installed `System/version` or `Module/version` to decide
whether an update is available.

## Format
Semantic versioning: `"1.2.3"`

download.description:
The absolute URL of the archive to download.

## Examples
- `"https://example.com/packages/dnd5e-1.2.3.system"`

- SeeAlso: `downloadURL`

compatibility.description:
The range of app versions this package supports.

`nil` means the package declares no constraint and is treated as compatible with every
app version.

- SeeAlso: `Compatibility`, `isCompatible`

repository.description:
The source repository hosting the package, as an absolute URL string.

## Examples
- `"https://github.com/example/dnd5e-system"`

website.description: The package's homepage, as an absolute URL string.

description.description:
The full description of the package.

Marketing copy or the author's overview, shown on the package detail screen.

content.description:
A summary of what the package contains.

A human-readable inventory of the content, listed separately from `description`.

## Examples
- `"12 maps, 40 pages, 60 monsters"`

authors.description:
The people or organizations credited on this package.

- SeeAlso: `Author`

media.description:
Absolute URLs of the package's promotional images.

Entries are identified by filename: the one containing `cover.` is used as the cover
image and the one containing `banner.` as the banner.

- SeeAlso: `imageURL`, `bannerURL`

featured.description:
Whether the catalog highlights this package.

Featured packages are surfaced at the top of the browse screen.

modified.description:
When the catalog listing was last updated.

## Format
ISO 8601: `"2024-03-17T09:24:00Z"`

created.description:
When the catalog listing was first published.

## Format
ISO 8601: `"2023-11-02T14:05:00Z"`

PackageType.title: PackageType
PackageType.description: What kind of content a `Package` installs.
